title: 2 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom?
questions.correctAnswer: Joab the son of Zeruiah
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:1 states that Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom.

questions.question: What did Joab send to Tekoah to fetch?
questions.correctAnswer: A wise woman
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:2 says Joab sent to Tekoah and fetched a wise woman.

questions.question: What did Joab instruct the wise woman to do when she came to the king?
options: Feign herself to be a mourner
questions.correctAnswer: Feign herself to be a mourner
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:2 records Joab instructing the woman to feign herself to be a mourner and put on mourning apparel.

questions.question: How did the woman of Tekoah behave when she spoke to the king?
options: She fell on her face and did obeisance
questions.correctAnswer: She fell on her face and did obeisance
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:4 describes the woman falling on her face and doing obeisance when she spoke to the king.

questions.question: What was the woman's initial complaint to the king?
options: She was a widow whose husband was dead
She wanted to see her son
questions.correctAnswer: She was a widow whose husband was dead
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:5 states the woman told the king she was indeed a widow and her husband was dead.

questions.question: What happened between the woman's two sons?
options: They strove together and one killed the other
questions.correctAnswer: They strove together and one killed the other
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:6 explains that the two sons strove in the field and one smote the other and slew him.

questions.question: What did the family of the slain son demand from the woman?
options: To deliver the one who killed his brother
questions.correctAnswer: To deliver the one who killed his brother
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:7 states the family demanded that the woman deliver the son who killed his brother so they could kill him.

questions.question: What was the king's initial response to the woman’s story?
options: Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee
Bring the guilty son to me immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:8 records the king telling the woman to go to her house and that he would give charge concerning her.

questions.question: Who did the woman say the iniquity belonged to?
options: On her and her father's house
questions.correctAnswer: On her and her father's house
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:9 records the woman saying the iniquity was on her and her father's house, not on the king or his throne.

questions.question: What did the king promise regarding anyone who harmed the woman?
options: They shall not touch her any more
They shall be punished by death
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not touch her any more
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:10 states the king said whoever harmed her should be brought to him and they would not touch her anymore.

questions.question: True or False: The king vowed that not one hair of the woman's son would fall to the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:11 records the king saying, 'As the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.'

questions.question: True or False: The woman of Tekoah claimed the king was at fault for not bringing back his banished.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:13 shows the woman saying the king speaks as one faulty for not fetching home again his banished.

questions.question: True or False: The woman said God devises means so that the banished are not expelled from Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:14 states that God devises means that the banished be not expelled from Him.

questions.question: True or False: The woman of Tekoah said she came to the king because she feared the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:15 states that the woman came to the king because the people had made her afraid, but she said it was to speak to the king that he might perform her request. The statement 'she came because she feared the people' is partially true, but the question as phrased implies only fear was the reason, which is misleading.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 14, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Joab sends for a wise woman to feign mourning
The woman speaks to the king and tells her story
The king commands Joab to bring Absalom back
Absalom sets Joab's field on fire
questions.correctAnswer: Joab sends for a wise woman to feign mourning
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:2 shows Joab first sending to Tekoah to fetch a wise woman before any other event occurs in the chapter.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What reason does the woman give for speaking to the king in 2 Samuel 14:15?
options: She was afraid of the people
questions.correctAnswer: She was afraid of the people
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 14:15, the woman explains that she came to speak to the king because the people had made her afraid, prompting her to hope the king would fulfill her request. This shows her motivation was fear of the people, not command or personal gain.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 14:14, why does God devise means regarding the banished?
options: To ensure they are not expelled from Him
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure they are not expelled from Him
questions.explanation: Verse 14 teaches that although people die and are like water spilled on the ground, God devises ways so that the banished are not expelled from Him. This shows God's mercy and care for the outcast.

questions.question: How does the king respond when the woman asks him to remember the LORD in 2 Samuel 14:11?
options: He promises no hair of her son shall fall to the earth
He orders her son to be killed
questions.correctAnswer: He promises no hair of her son shall fall to the earth
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 14:11, the king assures the woman that as the LORD lives, no hair of her son will fall to the ground, showing his commitment to protect her son and act mercifully.

questions.question: What does the woman say about the king's wisdom in 2 Samuel 14:17?
options: He is like an angel of God discerning good and bad
He is unaware of the people's needs
questions.correctAnswer: He is like an angel of God discerning good and bad
questions.explanation: Verse 17 praises the king's wisdom by comparing him to an angel of God who discerns good and bad, indicating confidence that God is with him and guiding his judgments.

questions.question: What does the king ask the woman in 2 Samuel 14:19?
options: If she is loyal to Absalom
If Joab's hand is involved in her story
If she wants to marry the king
questions.correctAnswer: If Joab's hand is involved in her story
questions.explanation: In verse 19, the king directly asks if Joab is behind the woman's words. She confirms Joab's involvement, showing Joab's role in orchestrating the plea to bring Absalom back.

questions.question: What does the king command Joab to do in 2 Samuel 14:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Bring Absalom back to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 21 records the king's direct command to Joab to bring Absalom back, showing his decision to restore Absalom despite previous exile.

questions.question: How does Joab express his gratitude to the king in 2 Samuel 14:22?
options: He falls on his face and thanks the king
questions.correctAnswer: He falls on his face and thanks the king
questions.explanation: Joab humbly bows to the ground and thanks the king for granting his request (verse 22), showing respect and relief that Absalom will return.

questions.question: What does the woman mean by saying 'the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty' in 2 Samuel 14:13?
options: The king is wise and just
The king is mistaken for not bringing back his banished
The king is angry with the people
The king is planning a war
questions.correctAnswer: The king is mistaken for not bringing back his banished
questions.explanation: The woman points out in verse 13 that the king wrongly judges by not bringing back those who are banished, implying the king's decision is flawed in this matter.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 14:16, the king will not listen to pleas to deliver from the hands of those who would destroy inheritance.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 16 explicitly states that the king will hear to deliver the woman and her son from the man who would destroy them, showing his willingness to intervene.

questions.question: How does the woman describe the danger she faces in 2 Samuel 14:7?
options: Her family wants to kill her surviving son and destroy her husband's name
She is threatened by foreign enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Her family wants to kill her surviving son and destroy her husband's name
questions.explanation: Verse 7 reveals the woman's family demands the death of her surviving son to avenge his brother's death, threatening to extinguish her husband's lineage.

questions.question: What does the king promise regarding anyone who harms the woman in 2 Samuel 14:10?
options: They shall not touch her anymore if brought to the king
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not touch her anymore if brought to the king
questions.explanation: In verse 10, the king commands that anyone who wrongs the woman be brought before him and shall not harm her again, showing royal protection.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Samuel 14:20, the woman credits Joab with orchestrating the entire speech and commends the king's wisdom.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states that Joab arranged the speech and the woman praises the king's wisdom as being like that of an angel of God, affirming both Joab's role and the king's discernment.

questions.question: What does the king ask the woman to do in 2 Samuel 14:18?
options: Not to hide anything, but to speak freely
questions.correctAnswer: Not to hide anything, but to speak freely
questions.explanation: In verse 18, the king encourages the woman not to conceal what he is about to ask, inviting openness and honest dialogue.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is demonstrated by the king when he agrees to bring Absalom back (2 Samuel 14:21-23)?
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness and restoration
questions.explanation: By ordering Absalom's return, the king models forgiveness and restoration, showing grace despite Absalom's previous wrongdoing (verses 21-23).

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 14:22, Joab knows he has found favor with the king because the king fulfilled his request.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 22 records Joab thanking the king and acknowledging that he has found grace because the king granted his request to bring Absalom back.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who brought Absalom back to Jerusalem after his exile in Geshur?
questions.correctAnswer: Joab
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 14:23, Joab arose and went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

questions.question: What restriction did King David place on Absalom upon his return to Jerusalem?
options: He was not allowed to see the king's face
He was made commander of the army
He was sent to another city
questions.correctAnswer: He was not allowed to see the king's face
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:24 states that David allowed Absalom to return to his house but told him not to see the king's face.

questions.question: How is Absalom described physically in 2 Samuel 14?
options: No blemish from head to foot
questions.correctAnswer: No blemish from head to foot
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:25 praises Absalom’s beauty, stating there was no blemish from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.

questions.question: How often did Absalom trim his hair, and what was notable about it?
options: Every year, his hair weighed 200 shekels
Every month, his hair was very light
Only once in his lifetime, hair was short
questions.correctAnswer: Every year, his hair weighed 200 shekels
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:26 explains Absalom cut his hair at the year's end because it was heavy, weighing 200 shekels by the king's weight standard.

questions.question: What was the name of Absalom's daughter, and how is she described?
options: Tamar, a woman of fair countenance
questions.correctAnswer: Tamar, a woman of fair countenance
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:27 mentions Absalom's daughter named Tamar, described as a woman of fair countenance.

questions.question: For how long did Absalom stay in Jerusalem without seeing the king's face after his return?
questions.correctAnswer: Two years
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:28 states Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem and saw not the king's face.

questions.question: What did Absalom do to compel Joab to come to him when Joab initially refused?
options: Set Joab's barley field on fire
Sent a messenger to the king
questions.correctAnswer: Set Joab's barley field on fire
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:30 recounts how Absalom's servants set Joab's barley field on fire to provoke Joab to come to him.

questions.question: What reason did Absalom give Joab for wanting to see the king's face?
options: To ask why he was banished and if guilty, to be killed
questions.correctAnswer: To ask why he was banished and if guilty, to be killed
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 14:32, Absalom tells Joab he wants to see the king's face to find out why he left Geshur and says if he is guilty, let him be killed.

questions.question: What was King David's reaction when Absalom finally came before him and bowed down?
questions.correctAnswer: He kissed Absalom
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:33 records that David kissed Absalom after he bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of restoring a banished son as seen in 2 Samuel 14?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 15:11-32 (Parable of the Prodigal Son)
questions.explanation: The theme of restoration and forgiveness of a banished son in 2 Samuel 14 is echoed in Luke 15:11-32, which tells the Parable of the Prodigal Son.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'poll' as used in the context of Absalom cutting his hair?
options: To cut or shear the hair
questions.correctAnswer: To cut or shear the hair
questions.explanation: The Hebrew verb translated as 'poll' refers to cutting or shearing hair, as seen in 2 Samuel 14:26 describing Absalom’s yearly hair cutting.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified by the wise woman's story about the two sons in 2 Samuel 14?
questions.correctAnswer: Parable
questions.explanation: The wise woman uses a parable (2 Samuel 14:6-14) to illustrate the injustice of Absalom’s banishment, a story designed to persuade the king.

questions.question: True or False: King David immediately allowed Absalom to see his face upon his return to Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:24 and 14:28 state that David allowed Absalom to return to his house but did not allow him to see his face for two years.

questions.question: True or False: Joab orchestrated the wise woman's plan to persuade King David to bring Absalom back from exile.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:19-20 clearly shows Joab's involvement in devising the wise woman's speech to influence the king’s decision.

questions.question: What does the episode of Absalom's hair weighing two hundred shekels symbolize in the ancient Near Eastern cultural context?
questions.correctAnswer: His strength and virility
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, long heavy hair was often a symbol of strength and virility, as Absalom's heavy hair (2 Samuel 14:26) implies his physical and social power.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by the king's promise that not one hair of the widow's son would fall to the ground?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:11 shows the king pledging protection over the widow’s son, reflecting God’s attribute of mercy in safeguarding life and showing compassion.

questions.question: How does the narrative of the wise woman of Tekoah in 2 Samuel 14 illustrate the doctrine of sanctification?
options: It shows God’s people are called to wise discernment and peacemaking
It teaches that mourning is the highest form of worship
It emphasizes strict legalism in judgment
It supports the idea that only kings can mediate grace
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s people are called to wise discernment and peacemaking
questions.explanation: The woman’s wise and strategic speech in 2 Samuel 14:2-4 reveals the sanctified use of wisdom and peacemaking to restore relationships, reflecting the believer’s call to holiness in actions.

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by the king’s instruction to protect the widow from the revengers of blood in 2 Samuel 14?
options: Doctrine of justice tempered by mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of justice tempered by mercy
questions.explanation: The king’s protective charge in 2 Samuel 14:10-11 reveals the balance of justice and mercy, a key biblical doctrine where God’s justice is softened by compassion.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from the widow’s claim that God ‘doth devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him’ (2 Samuel 14:14) combined with the king’s eventual restoration of Absalom?
options: God’s plan includes restoration and reconciliation for the repentant
God’s justice is irrevocable without repentance
God’s covenant only applies to the king’s family
questions.correctAnswer: God’s plan includes restoration and reconciliation for the repentant
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 14:14 and 14:21 together teach that God’s providential design includes restoring those who are estranged, highlighting the doctrine of reconciliation and grace.

questions.question: How does Absalom’s refusal to see the king’s face for two years (2 Samuel 14:24, 28) reflect on the human condition and the need for divine intervention?
options: It shows human alienation due to sin requiring God’s restorative work
It indicates human self-sufficiency apart from God
It demonstrates that physical separation cures sin
It reveals the futility of forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human alienation due to sin requiring God’s restorative work
questions.explanation: Absalom’s estrangement (2 Samuel 14:24, 28) typifies the alienation caused by sin, emphasizing the need for divine mediation and restoration, a core biblical theme about human brokenness.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in the king’s wisdom to discern good and bad as described by the woman in 2 Samuel 14:17?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wisdom
questions.explanation: The woman’s comparison of the king’s discernment to that of an angel of God in 2 Samuel 14:17 underscores God’s attribute of wisdom manifested through His anointed ruler.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 14:13-14, what theological truth is taught about human mortality and God’s impartiality?
options: All humans must die and God shows no partiality
Only kings are granted long life
Death is a punishment for sinners alone
questions.correctAnswer: All humans must die and God shows no partiality
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 teach that death is universal and that God does not respect persons, meaning He is impartial in judgment, which is a foundational doctrine about God’s justice and human mortality.

questions.question: What does the sovereignty of God over human affairs emerge from Joab’s orchestration of Absalom’s return (2 Samuel 14:1-3, 21-23)?
options: God sovereignly uses human agents to accomplish His purposes
Human plans always thwart God’s will
God delegates authority only to kings
Human wisdom is superior to divine wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses human agents to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Joab’s strategic intervention (2 Samuel 14:1-3, 21-23) illustrates how God sovereignly works through human actions and decisions to bring about His redemptive plans.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Absalom’s hair weighing two hundred shekels (2 Samuel 14:26) typologically relate to biblical themes of pride and downfall?
options: Beauty is irrelevant in biblical narratives
questions.correctAnswer: Excessive pride often precedes judgment
questions.explanation: Absalom’s heavy hair (2 Samuel 14:26) foreshadows his pride and eventual downfall, echoing biblical patterns where outward beauty and pride lead to tragic judgment (cf. Proverbs 16:18).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Samuel 14:5-7 and 2 Samuel 14:11 provide about the nature of justice and intercession?
options: Justice requires protection of the innocent and intercession can mitigate judgment
Justice is absolute and leaves no room for mercy
Intercession is unnecessary when justice is served
The innocent must suffer for the guilty
questions.correctAnswer: Justice requires protection of the innocent and intercession can mitigate judgment
questions.explanation: Together, these verses show that justice involves protecting the innocent (the widow’s remaining son) and that intercession (the widow’s plea) can influence the application of justice, reflecting God’s merciful justice.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the story in 2 Samuel 14 promotes political manipulation rather than divine truth. What does 2 Samuel 14:19-21 actually teach about divine wisdom working through human actions?
options: God’s wisdom can be mediated through human strategy to fulfill His purposes
Human manipulation is superior to divine guidance
Divine truth is separate from human involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wisdom can be mediated through human strategy to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 19-21 reveal that Joab’s counsel and the king’s response demonstrate God’s providential use of human actions and wisdom to accomplish His will, countering sceptical claims of mere manipulation.

questions.question: What does the king’s kiss of Absalom after his return (2 Samuel 14:33) signify in biblical theology?
questions.correctAnswer: Restoration of relationship and forgiveness
questions.explanation: The king’s kiss in 2 Samuel 14:33 symbolizes restored fellowship and forgiveness, reflecting the biblical theme of reconciliation between God and sinners (cf. Luke 15:20).

questions.question: How does the widow’s plea in 2 Samuel 14:15-16 combined with the king’s response illustrate the doctrine of God’s providence?
options: God orchestrates events to protect His inheritance and people
God leaves people to fend for themselves
Providence depends solely on human effort
Divine providence is unpredictable and random
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates events to protect His inheritance and people
questions.explanation: The widow’s appeal and the king’s protection (2 Samuel 14:15-16) demonstrate God’s providential care in preserving His people and their inheritance against destruction.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does the banishment and return of Absalom in 2 Samuel 14 have with the overall biblical story of redemption?
options: It prefigures themes of exile and restoration central to the Messiah’s work
It is unrelated to the broader biblical narrative
It denies the possibility of forgiveness
It focuses only on political intrigue
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures themes of exile and restoration central to the Messiah’s work
questions.explanation: Absalom’s exile and return in 2 Samuel 14 mirror the larger redemptive themes of exile and restoration culminating in Christ’s work to reconcile sinners to God (cf. Isaiah 53).

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by the woman’s statement that God ‘doth not respect any person’ in 2 Samuel 14:14?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s impartiality in judgment
questions.explanation: The declaration in 2 Samuel 14:14 that God does not respect persons reveals the doctrine that God judges all people impartially, without favoritism or partiality.
